summary: Holy animals that became unfit are sold in the market like regular meat, because the money goes to hekdesh. A bechor and ma'aser are not sold that way, because the money goes to their owners.

chunks.en: All holy animals that became unfit, whose money goes to hekdesh,
chunks.st: With regard to all disqualified consecrated animals that were disqualified for sacrifice due to blemishes and were redeemed, all benefit accrued from their sale belongs to the Temple
chunks.stMore: treasury. In order to ensure that the Temple treasury will not suffer a loss, these animals

chunks.en: are sold in the meat market, shechted in the market, and weighed by the litra,
chunks.st: are sold in the butchers’ market [ba’itliz] and slaughtered in the butchers’ market, where the demand is great and the price is consequently higher. And their meat is weighed and sold by the litra,
chunks.stMore: in the manner that non-sacred meat is sold. This is the halakha with regard to all consecrated animals

words.note: A measure of weight, like a pound.

chunks.en: except for a bechor and ma'aser,
chunks.st: except for the firstborn offering and an animal tithe
chunks.stMore: offering. When these become blemished and their slaughter is permitted, they are sold and slaughtered only in the owner’s house and are not weighed; rather, they are sold by estimate.

chunks.en: because their money goes to the owners.
chunks.st: The reason is that all benefit accrued from their sale belongs to the owner,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the priest in the case of the firstborn and the owner in the case of the animal tithe offering. It is not permitted to treat disqualified consecrated animals as one treats non-sacred animals merely to guarantee that the owner will receive the optimal price.

chunks.en: The money of unfit holy animals goes to hekdesh.
chunks.st: This is in contrast to disqualified consecrated animals, where all benefit accrued from their sale belongs to the Temple
chunks.stMore: treasury, and therefore the animal is sold in the market to ensure that the optimal price is received.

words.note: The treasury of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: But one may weigh one piece against another piece of a bechor.
chunks.st: And although the meat of the firstborn is not weighed and sold by the litra, nevertheless, if one has non-sacred meat weighing one hundred dinars, one may weigh one portion of non-sacred meat against one portion of the meat of the firstborn,
chunks.stMore: because that is unlike the manner in which non-sacred meat is weighed.

summary: Who may eat from a bechor with a blemish, and whether we may let blood from a bechor that is sick, even if this makes a blemish.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.he: לֹא יִמָּנָה יִשְׂרָאֵל עִם הַכֹּהֵן עַל הַבְּכוֹר.
chunks.en: a Yisrael may not join with a Kohen to eat a bechor.
chunks.st: An Israelite cannot be counted with the priest to partake of a blemished firstborn.

chunks.en: Beis Hillel allow it,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel deem it permitted for him to partake of it,

chunks.en: and even a non-Jew.
chunks.st: and they deem it permitted even for a gentile
chunks.stMore: to partake of a blemished firstborn. With regard to

chunks.en: A bechor that has too much blood in it,
chunks.st: a firstborn animal that was congested with excess blood,

chunks.en: even if it will die,
chunks.st: even if the animal will die if one does not let the excess blood,

chunks.en: we do not let out its blood.
chunks.st: one may not let its blood,
chunks.stMore: as this might cause a blemish, and it is prohibited to cause a blemish on consecrated animals. This is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Yehudah says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: יַקִּיז, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲשֶׂה בוֹ מוּם.
chunks.en: he may let its blood, as long as he does not make a blemish.
chunks.st: One may let the blood provided that he will not cause a blemish while doing so,

chunks.en: And if he did make a blemish,
chunks.st: and if he caused a blemish,

chunks.en: he may not shecht it because of that blemish.
chunks.st: the animal may not be slaughtered on account of that
chunks.stMore: blemish. Since he was the cause of the blemish, he may not slaughter the animal until it develops a different, unrelated blemish.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says, he may let its blood,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says: One may let the blood

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה בוֹ מוּם:
chunks.en: even if he makes a blemish.
chunks.st: even if he thereby causes a blemish in the animal.

summary: If a person makes a blemish on a bechor on purpose, he may not shecht it because of that blemish. Two stories show the rule: a blemish made on purpose is forbidden, and one made by accident is allowed.

chunks.en: Someone who cuts the ear of a bechor:
chunks.st: In the case of one who slits [hatzorem] the ear of a firstborn offering,

chunks.en: it may never be shechted.
chunks.st: that person may never slaughter that animal. This is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Eliezer says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: when it gets a different blemish,
chunks.st: If another blemish later develops in the firstborn,

chunks.en: it may be shechted because of that one.
chunks.st: he may slaughter the animal on account of that second blemish.

chunks.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְזָכָר שֶׁל רְחֵלִים זָקֵן וּשְׂעָרוֹ מְדֻלְדָּל,
chunks.en: Once there was an old ram whose wool hung down long.
chunks.st: There was an incident involving an old ram whose hair was long and dangling, because it was a firstborn offering.

chunks.en: A Roman officer saw it
chunks.st: And one Roman quaestor [kastor] saw it

chunks.en: and said, "What is this one about?"
chunks.st: and said to its owner: What is the status [tivo] of this
chunks.stMore: animal that you allowed it to grow old and you did not slaughter it?

chunks.en: They told him,
chunks.st: They said to him:

chunks.en: "It is a bechor, and it may be shechted only
chunks.st: It is a firstborn offering, and therefore it may be slaughtered only

chunks.en: if it has a blemish."
chunks.st: if it has a blemish.

chunks.en: He took a dagger and cut its ear.
chunks.st: The quaestor took a dagger [pigom] and slit its ear.

chunks.en: The case came before the Sages, and they allowed it.
chunks.st: And the incident came before the Sages for a ruling, and they deemed its slaughter permitted.

chunks.en: When he saw that they allowed it,
chunks.st: And after the Sages deemed its slaughter permitted,

chunks.he: וְהָלַךְ וְצָרַם בְּאָזְנֵי בְכוֹרוֹת אֲחֵרִים, וְאָסָרוּ.
chunks.en: he went and cut the ears of other bechoros, and the Sages forbade them.
chunks.st: the quaestor went and slit the ears of other firstborn offerings, but in these cases the Sages deemed their slaughter prohibited,
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that they were now blemished.

chunks.he: פַּעַם אַחַת הָיוּ תִינוֹקוֹת מְשַׂחֲקִין בַּשָּׂדֶה
chunks.en: One time, children were playing in the field
chunks.st: One time children were playing in the field

chunks.en: and tied the tails of lambs to each other,
chunks.st: and they tied the tails of lambs to each other,

chunks.en: and the tail of one of them came off,
chunks.st: and the tail of one of them was severed,

chunks.en: and it was a bechor.
chunks.st: and it was a firstborn offering.

chunks.en: The case came before the Sages, and they allowed it.
chunks.st: And the incident came before the Sages for a ruling and they deemed its slaughter permitted.

chunks.en: When people saw that they allowed it,
chunks.st: The people who saw that they deemed its slaughter permitted

chunks.he: וְהָלְכוּ וְקָשְׁרוּ זַנְבוֹת בְּכוֹרוֹת אֲחֵרִים, וְאָסָרוּ.
chunks.en: they went and tied the tails of other bechoros, and the Sages forbade them.
chunks.st: went and tied the tails of other firstborn offerings, and the Sages deemed their slaughter prohibited.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: any blemish made on purpose is forbidden,
chunks.st: With regard to any blemish that is caused intentionally, the animal’s slaughter is prohibited;

chunks.en: and one made not on purpose is allowed.
chunks.st: if the blemish is caused unintentionally, the animal’s slaughter is permitted.

summary: If a bechor got a blemish by accident, it may be shechted. The Rabbis argue whether a Kohen shepherd can be believed that a blemish was not made on purpose.

chunks.en: If a bechor was chasing him,
chunks.st: If one’s firstborn offering was pursuing him,

chunks.en: and he kicked it and made a blemish,
chunks.st: and he kicked the animal and caused a blemish in it,

chunks.en: he may shecht it because of that blemish.
chunks.st: he may slaughter the animal on account of that blemish.

chunks.he: כָּל הַמּוּמִין הָרְאוּיִין לָבוֹא בִידֵי אָדָם,
chunks.en: For all blemishes that a person could make,
chunks.st: With regard to all the blemishes that are capable of being brought about by a person,

chunks.en: shepherds who are Yisraelim are believed,
chunks.st: Israelite shepherds are deemed credible
chunks.stMore: to testify that the blemishes were not caused intentionally.

chunks.en: but shepherds who are Kohanim are not believed.
chunks.st: But priest-shepherds are not deemed credible,
chunks.stMore: as they are the beneficiaries if the firstborn is blemished.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: a Kohen is believed about his friend's animal
chunks.st: A priest is deemed credible to testify about the firstborn of another,

chunks.en: but not about his own.
chunks.st: but is not deemed credible to testify about the firstborn belonging to him.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: someone suspected about a thing
chunks.st: A priest who is suspect about the matter of causing a blemish

chunks.en: may not judge it and may not be a witness about it.
chunks.st: may neither adjudicate nor testify
chunks.stMore: in cases involving that matter, even on behalf of another.

summary: Who is believed about a blemish, and when a bechor with a clear blemish may be shechted without asking an expert.

chunks.en: A Kohen is believed to say, "I showed this bechor
chunks.st: A priest is deemed credible to say: I showed this firstborn

chunks.en: to an expert, and it has a blemish."
chunks.st: animal to an expert and he ruled that it is blemished.

chunks.en: Everyone is believed about blemishes of ma'aser animals.
chunks.st: Everyone is deemed credible to testify about the blemishes of an animal tithe
chunks.stMore: offering, even the owner who is the beneficiary of a ruling that it is blemished.

chunks.en: A bechor whose eye became blind,
chunks.st: With regard to a firstborn animal whose eye was blinded

chunks.en: whose front leg was cut off,
chunks.st: or whose foreleg was severed

chunks.en: or whose back leg was broken:
chunks.st: or whose hind leg was broken,
chunks.stMore: all of which obviously render the animal permanently blemished, that animal

chunks.en: it may be shechted by the word
chunks.st: may be slaughtered on the basis of the ruling of

chunks.en: of three people from the shul.
chunks.st: three regular Jews who attend the synagogue,
chunks.stMore: and it does not require a ruling by one of the Sages.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei disagrees and says:

chunks.en: even if twenty-three judges are there,
chunks.st: Even if there is a court of twenty-three Sages there,

chunks.he: לֹא יִשָּׁחֵט אֶלָּא עַל פִּי מֻמְחֶה:
chunks.en: it may be shechted only by the word of an expert.
chunks.st: it may be slaughtered only on the basis of the ruling of an expert in judging blemishes.

summary: If someone sold meat of a bechor that was not checked by an expert, or meat that turned out to be treif, he must give the money back.

chunks.en: Someone shechted a bechor and sold it,
chunks.st: In the case of one who slaughters a firstborn animal and sells its meat,

chunks.en: and then they found out that he did not show it to an expert:
chunks.st: and it was discovered that he did not initially show it
chunks.stMore: to one of the Sages, the halakha is that it was actually prohibited to derive any benefit from the meat.

chunks.en: what they ate, they ate,
chunks.st: In that case, what the buyers ate, they ate,

chunks.en: and he must give them back the money.
chunks.st: and the Sages penalized the seller in that he must return the money to them, which they paid for the meat that they ate.

chunks.en: And what they did not eat:
chunks.st: And with regard to that which they did not eat,

chunks.en: the meat must be buried,
chunks.st: that meat must be buried,

chunks.en: and he must give them back the money.
chunks.st: and he must return the money
chunks.stMore: that they paid for the meat that they did not eat.

chunks.en: The same if someone shechted a cow
chunks.st: And likewise, in the case of one who slaughters a cow

chunks.en: and sold it, and they found out it was treif:
chunks.st: and sells it, and it was discovered that it is a tereifa,

words.note: An animal with a deadly injury, which may not be eaten.

chunks.he: מַה שֶׁאָכְלוּ אָכְלוּ וְיַחֲזִיר לָהֶם אֶת הַדָּמִים.
chunks.en: what they ate, they ate, and he must give them back the money.
chunks.st: what the buyers ate, they ate,

chunks.en: And what they did not eat:
chunks.st: and what they did not eat,

chunks.en: they give him back the meat,
chunks.st: they must return the meat to
chunks.stMore: the seller, who may sell it to a gentile or feed it to the dogs,

chunks.en: and he gives them back the money.
chunks.st: and he must return the money to the buyers.

chunks.en: If they sold it to non-Jews or threw it to the dogs,
chunks.st: If the buyers sold it to gentiles or cast it to the dogs,

chunks.en: they must pay him what treif meat is worth.
chunks.st: they pay the seller the value of a tereifa,
chunks.stMore: which is less than the value of kosher meat, and the seller refunds the balance to the buyers.
